## Client

`new Xyte(options)` and its methods. Topic pages: [configuration](configuration.md), [the client's lifecycle](lifecycle.md).

### `Xyte`

The client: Zyte API's `POST /v1/extract` through the providers you choose.

```ts
const xyte = new Xyte({ proxy: oxylabs({ username, password }) });
const page = await xyte.extract({ url, httpResponseBody: true });
```

Close it when done if it rendered pages (see docs/lifecycle.md).

```ts
class Xyte {
  constructor(options?: XyteOptions);
  /**
   * Same contract as `POST https://api.zyte.com/v1/extract`: resolves with the 200 body, rejects
   * with an `XyteError` carrying Zyte's status and problem type.
   */
  extract(request: ExtractRequest, options?: ExtractOptions): Promise<ExtractResponse>;
  /**
   * Many requests, as they finish: `for await (const r of xyte.extractMany(urls.map(…)))`. Takes
   * any iterable or async iterable (a list, a file read line by line, a queue), keeps at most
   * `concurrency` in flight (default: the client's, else 16), and yields `{ index, request,
   * response }` or `{ index, request, error }`: one failure doesn't stop the batch. The client's
   * `concurrency`, `rateLimits`, cache and reports apply to each request as usual. Leaving the
   * loop early (`break`, `return`, an exception) cancels the requests still in flight.
   */
  extractMany(requests: Iterable<ExtractRequest> | AsyncIterable<ExtractRequest>, options?: {
    concurrency?: number;
    signal?: AbortSignal;
  }): AsyncGenerator<BatchResult>;
  /** `extractMany()` collected, in the order of `requests`. */
  extractAll(requests: Iterable<ExtractRequest> | AsyncIterable<ExtractRequest>, options?: {
    concurrency?: number;
    signal?: AbortSignal;
  }): Promise<BatchResult[]>;
  /**
   * Cancels the requests in flight (they reject with a `/client/closed` error), waits for them to
   * settle, then closes the shared browser, if one was started. Safe to call more than once, and
   * the client keeps working afterwards: the next render launches a new browser.
   */
  close(): Promise<void>;
  /** What makes `await using xyte = new Xyte(…)` work: calls `close()` when the block ends (docs/lifecycle.md). */
  [Symbol.asyncDispose](): Promise<void>;
}
```

### `createXyte`

Shorthand for `new Xyte(options)`.

```ts
function createXyte(options?: XyteOptions): Xyte;
```

### `XyteOptions`

Options of `new Xyte()`. Everything is optional: `new Xyte()` makes direct requests.

```ts
interface XyteOptions {
  /** Where requests exit. Default: `direct()` (no proxy). */
  proxy?: ProxyProvider;
  /**
   * Retries after a ban, a proxy failure or a network error, each through a fresh session
   * (a new exit IP). Default 3, like Zyte's own clients.
   */
  retries?: number;
  /** Per-attempt timeout, seconds. Default 60. */
  timeout?: number;
  /** Max requests in flight; extra calls queue. Default: unlimited. */
  concurrency?: number;
  /**
   * Decides whether a downloaded page is a ban (retried, then a 520) rather than the real page.
   * Default: `isLikelyBan`. Pass `false` to return every page as is.
   */
  isBan?: ((page: BanCheck) => boolean) | false;
  /** Browser rendering for `browserHtml`, `screenshot`, `actions`, `networkCapture`. */
  browser?: BrowserOptions;
  /**
   * Handlers for Zyte's own actions outside Zyte: `searchKeyword` (default: a heuristic that
   * finds the search box), `setLocation` (per site), `interaction` (scripts by id). With
   * `zyteApi()` as the provider, Zyte runs them instead.
   */
  actions?: ActionHandlers;
  /**
   * What happens to an action that can't run where the attempt landed: a Zyte-only action with
   * no handler on a local-browser provider (proxies, `direct()`, remote browsers), or any action
   * on an HTML-only API (Scrappey, ScrapingBot), once there's no provider to pass over to.
   * `warn` (default) skips it (`notExecuted` in the response's `actions`, plus a warning) and runs
   * the rest; `error` passes over to `zyteApi()` when a combinator has it, else rejects with a
   * 400; `zyte` passes over to `zyteApi()` when a combinator has it (the built-in search
   * heuristic's actions too), else like `warn`. Actions you have a handler for always run locally.
   * See docs/actions.md.
   */
  unsupportedActions?: "warn" | "error" | "zyte";
  /**
   * Implementations for Zyte's extraction outputs (`product`, `article`, `markdown`, …), keyed by
   * field. Requests for a field without an extractor are rejected with a 400, except `markdown`,
   * which has a built-in (non-AI, like Zyte's) converter.
   */
  extractors?: Partial<Record<ExtractionField, Extractor>>;
  /** Server-managed sessions (`sessionContext`): pool size, max age, bans before retiring. */
  sessions?: SessionPoolOptions;
  /** Low-level HTTP sender; replace to add logging, or for tests. */
  transport?: Transport;
  /** Called before each retry. */
  onRetry?: (info: {
    attempt: number;
    url: string;
    reason: string;
  }) => void;
  /**
   * Called after every attempt with the provider that served it (the one a combinator picked),
   * the outcome, latency and page size: per-provider success rates and costs, in your metrics.
   */
  onAttempt?: (info: AttemptInfo) => void;
  /**
   * Called once per `extract()`, success or failure, with what it took: every attempt (provider,
   * route, result, latency, bytes), totals per provider, and the outcome. For logs, metrics and
   * analytics; the response itself stays Zyte's.
   */
  onRequest?: (report: RequestReport) => void;
  /**
   * Keep responses for a while and answer repeats from them (and let identical requests in flight
   * share one run): `{ ttl: 3600 }`, or per site `{ ttl: { 'wolt.com': 600, '*': 3600 } }`.
   * Requests with a `session` or `sessionContext` are never cached. Off by default.
   */
  cache?: CacheOptions;
  /**
   * How fast, and how many at once, attempts go to each site: `{ 'yelp.co.uk': '2/s', '*': '10/s' }`
   * (each site under `'*'` on its own), or `{ rate, per, concurrency }`. Per process. Off by default.
   */
  rateLimits?: RateLimits;
  /**
   * Your prices, per provider (its name, or a prefix: `oxylabs` covers `oxylabs-residential`):
   * `{ oxylabs: { perGB: 6 }, 'zyte-api': { perRequest: 0.0013 } }`. Attempts and reports then
   * carry `costUsd`. Plans and volume discounts differ, so there are no built-in prices.
   */
  rates?: Rates;
  /**
   * When a plain HTTP request (GET, no body) is banned, retry it in a browser, which gets past
   * JavaScript challenges, and return the page's raw HTTP response as `httpResponseBody`, as
   * Zyte does when it picks a browser itself. Needs Playwright (or `browser.connect`). Default false.
   */
  browserFallback?: boolean;
  /**
   * Requests that run but not as asked, e.g. a `geolocation` the exit can't apply (`direct()`,
   * a plain proxy URL). Default: `console.warn`, once per distinct message.
   */
  onWarning?: (message: string, info: {
    url: string;
  }) => void;
}
```

### `ExtractOptions`

Per-call options of `extract()`.

```ts
interface ExtractOptions {
  /** Aborts the request (all attempts). Rejects with the signal's reason. */
  signal?: AbortSignal;
  /** This request's warnings, in addition to the client's `onWarning`. */
  onWarning?: (message: string) => void;
  /** This request's report once it's done, in addition to the client's `onRequest`. */
  onReport?: (report: RequestReport) => void;
}
```

### `BatchResult`

One request of `extractMany()`: its position, and its response or the error it failed with.

```ts
interface BatchResult {
  index: number;
  request: ExtractRequest;
  response?: ExtractResponse;
  error?: unknown;
}
```

### `decodeBody`

An `httpResponseBody` (or a `networkCapture` body) as UTF-8 text. Bodies are base64 in Zyte's
API, because they can be anything (an image, a PDF):

```ts
const page = await xyte.extract({ url, httpResponseBody: true });
const html = decodeBody(page.httpResponseBody!);
```

For binary content, decode to bytes instead: `Buffer.from(body, 'base64')`.

```ts
function decodeBody(base64: string): string;
```

### `Transport`

Sends one HTTP request, never following redirects (the HTTP engine does that itself).

```ts
type Transport = (request: TransportRequest) => Promise<Response>;
```

### `TransportRequest`

One HTTP request as a `Transport` gets it: URL, method, headers, body, the proxy to go through, and a signal.

```ts
interface TransportRequest {
  url: string;
  method: string;
  headers: Headers;
  body?: Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer>;
  proxy: ProxyEndpoint | null;
  signal: AbortSignal;
}
```

### `SessionPoolOptions`

Zyte's server-managed sessions (`sessionContext`): requests with the same context share a
small pool of sessions, each initialized once with `sessionContextParameters` (a sticky exit
plus the cookies the init actions produced). Sessions expire after 4 hours or 3 bans.

```ts
interface SessionPoolOptions {
  /** Sessions per context. Default 8. */
  size?: number;
  /** Seconds before a session is retired. Default 4 h (Zyte's). */
  maxAge?: number;
  /** Bans (or failed attempts) before a session is retired. Default 3 (Zyte's). */
  maxBans?: number;
  /**
   * Shared state: every instance draws from the same sessions per context, with their cookies,
   * bans and whether they're initialized (a session another instance logged in isn't logged in
   * again). Default: this process only.
   */
  store?: StateStore;
  /** Seconds between re-reads of a context's shared sessions (before an acquire). Default 5. */
  syncEvery?: number;
}
```

## Requests, responses and errors

Zyte's request and response bodies, generated from Zyte's OpenAPI spec, and the errors `extract()` rejects with. Field by field: [coverage](coverage.md); errors: [the README](../README.md#errors-and-retries).

### `ExtractRequest`

The body of `POST https://api.zyte.com/v1/extract`.

Loosened from the spec where Zyte itself is lenient: `geolocation` in any case, the network
capture filters as the union the spec describes in prose, and `echoData` as any JSON.

```ts
type ExtractRequest = Omit<ZyteSchemas["ExtractRequest"], "geolocation" | "networkCapture" | "echoData" | "tags"> & {
  geolocation?: CountryCode | Lowercase<CountryCode>;
  networkCapture?: NetworkCaptureFilter[];
  echoData?: unknown;
  /** Labels for the request. "Values must be strings or `null`" (Zyte's docs; the schema says strings only). */
  tags?: Record<string, string | null>;
};
```

### `ExtractResponse`

The 200 body of `POST /v1/extract`.

```ts
type ExtractResponse = Omit<ZyteSchemas["Response200"], "echoData"> & {
  echoData?: unknown;
};
```

### `ExtractionField`

One of `EXTRACTION_FIELDS`: `product`, `article`, … `markdown`.

```ts
type ExtractionField = (typeof EXTRACTION_FIELDS)[number];
```

### `EXTRACTION_FIELDS`

Zyte's extraction outputs. `markdown` has a built-in converter; the others need an extractor (`extractors` option, or `llmExtractors()`).

```ts
const EXTRACTION_FIELDS: readonly ["product", "productList", "productNavigation", "article", "articleList", "articleNavigation", "forumThread", "jobPosting", "jobPostingNavigation", "pageContent", "serp", "customAttributes", "markdown"];
```

### `Action`

One browser action (`click`, `type`, `scrollBottom`, `waitForSelector`…), as in `actions`.

```ts
type Action = ZyteSchemas["ActionSequence"][number];
```

### `ActionName`

The name of an action: `click`, `type`, `searchKeyword`…

```ts
type ActionName = Action["action"];
```

### `ActionResult`

What happened to one action, in the response's `actions`: `status`, `error`, `elapsedTime`.

```ts
type ActionResult = ZyteSchemas["ActionResult"];
```

### `ActionSelector`

How an action finds its element: `{ type: 'css' | 'xpath', value }`.

```ts
type ActionSelector = ZyteSchemas["ActionSelector"];
```

### `Cookie`

A cookie, as in `requestCookies` and `responseCookies`.

```ts
type Cookie = ZyteSchemas["Cookie"];
```

### `HttpHeader`

A header as a `{ name, value }` pair, as Zyte lists them (`httpResponseHeaders`, `customHttpRequestHeaders`).

```ts
type HttpHeader = ZyteSchemas["HTTPHeader"];
```

### `CapturedResponse`

One response a browser render captured (`networkCapture`): its URL, status, headers and body.

```ts
type CapturedResponse = ZyteSchemas["CapturedResponse"];
```

### `NetworkCaptureFilter`

Which responses `networkCapture` keeps: by URL, or by resource type.

```ts
type NetworkCaptureFilter = ZyteSchemas["UrlFilter"] | ZyteSchemas["ResourceTypeFilter"];
```

### `CountryCode`

An ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, as `geolocation` takes (`US`, `DE`…).

```ts
type CountryCode = ZyteSchemas["CountryCode"];
```

### `Problem`

Zyte's error body as the spec has it. `XyteProblem` is the same with the fields xyte always sets.

```ts
type Problem = ZyteSchemas["Problem"];
```

### `ZyteSchemas`

Every schema of the Zyte API OpenAPI spec, as generated.

```ts
type ZyteSchemas = components["schemas"];
```

### `XyteError`

A Zyte API error response (RFC 7807 problem). `status` and `type` use the values Zyte uses
(https://docs.zyte.com/zyte-api/usage/errors.html), so code written against Zyte keeps working.

```ts
class XyteError extends Error {
  /** The HTTP status Zyte answers with: 400, 422, 429, 500, 520, 521… */
  readonly status: number;
  /** The problem type, the stable thing to branch on: `/download/website-ban`, `/request/invalid`… */
  readonly type: string;
  /** A short human-readable summary of the type. */
  readonly title: string;
  /** What went wrong for this request, when there's more to say. */
  readonly detail?: string;
  /** `retryable` overrides the status-based rule (a misconfiguration's 500 is not). */
  constructor(problem: XyteProblem, options?: {
    cause?: unknown;
    retryable?: boolean;
  });
  /** Worth retrying later, the same way Zyte's own clients retry. */
  get retryable(): boolean;
  /** The problem as Zyte's error body; what `xyte serve` answers with. */
  toJSON(): XyteProblem;
}
```

### `XyteProblem`

A Zyte error body (an RFC 7807 problem): `type`, `status`, `title` and an optional `detail`.

```ts
type XyteProblem = Required<Pick<Problem, "type" | "status" | "title">> & {
  detail?: string;
};
```

### `UpstreamProblem`

A retryable failure an upstream Zyte-compatible API answered with its own problem (a 520 ban,
a 429). Retried like any download error; if it is the last one, that problem is returned as is.

```ts
class UpstreamProblem extends Error {
  /** Always `UpstreamProblem`. */
  override name: string;
  /** The upstream's problem, returned to the caller as is if no retry succeeds. */
  readonly problem: XyteProblem;
  constructor(problem: XyteProblem);
}
```

### `isLikelyBan`

The default ban check: a 403, 429 or 503, or a 200 that is an anti-bot challenge page
(Cloudflare, DataDome, PerimeterX, Akamai…). Replace it with the `isBan` option.

```ts
function isLikelyBan(page: BanCheck): boolean;
```

### `BanCheck`

What the ban check (`isBan`) looks at: the target's answer to one attempt.

```ts
interface BanCheck {
  url: string;
  statusCode: number;
  headers: {
    name: string;
    value: string;
  }[];
  html?: string;
}
```

## Providers

Where requests exit. Every preset's credentials and options: [providers](providers.md).

### `direct`

No proxy: requests go straight from this machine.

```ts
function direct(): ProxyProvider<ProxyEndpoint>;
```

### `proxyUrl`

Any proxy (or list of proxies) given as URLs. With several, attempts rotate through them, so a
retry uses the next one. For providers that encode geo/session in the URL, use `custom`.

```ts
function proxyUrl(urls: string | readonly string[], options?: {
  insecure?: boolean;
}): ProxyProvider<ProxyEndpoint>;
```

### `template`

Any provider, from its URL format. Placeholders:

- `{country}` / `{country:lower}`: ISO-2 country from `geolocation`
- `{session}` / `{session:8}`: sticky-session token (alphanumeric, given length, default 12)
- `{session:number}` / `{session:number:99999}`: numeric session id (below the given max)
- `{ipType}`, `{attempt}`
- `{env:NAME}`: an environment variable (e.g. the password)

Square brackets mark an optional part, dropped when a placeholder inside has no value (no
`geolocation` on the request, say). Substituted values are URL-encoded; literal text is not.

    template('http://user-{env:USER}[-country-{country:lower}]-session-{session}:{env:PASS}@gate.example.com:7000')

```ts
function template(format: string, options?: {
  insecure?: boolean;
  name?: string;
}): ProxyProvider<ProxyEndpoint>;
```

### `custom`

Build the proxy URL yourself from the context.

```ts
function custom(name: string, resolve: (context: ProxyContext) => string | ProxyEndpoint | null | Promise<string | ProxyEndpoint | null>): ProxyProvider<ProxyEndpoint>;
```

### `proxyEndpointUrl`

A proxy URL with the credentials percent-encoded: `proxyEndpointUrl({ host: 'pr.oxylabs.io', port: 7777, username, password })`
→ `http://user:p%40ss@pr.oxylabs.io:7777`.

```ts
function proxyEndpointUrl(args: {
  host: string;
  port: number | string;
  username?: string;
  password?: string;
  protocol?: "http" | "https";
}): string;
```

### `oxylabs`

Oxylabs (https://developers.oxylabs.io/proxies/residential-proxies).
Residential: `customer-USER-cc-US-sessid-…-sesstime-10` on pr.oxylabs.io:7777.
Datacenter: `user-USER-country-US` on dc.oxylabs.io:8000.

```ts
function oxylabs(options: {
  username: string;
  password: string;
  type?: "residential" | "datacenter";
  host?: string;
  port?: number;
  /** Sticky session lifetime, minutes (residential, max 1440). Default 10. */
  sessionMinutes?: number;
}): ProxyProvider<ProxyEndpoint>;
```

### `brightData`

Bright Data (https://docs.brightdata.com/proxy-networks/config-options).
`brd-customer-ID-zone-ZONE-country-us-session-…` on brd.superproxy.io:33335.
Bright Data intercepts TLS unless your account is verified; pass `insecure: true` (or install
their CA) if you see certificate errors.

```ts
function brightData(options: {
  customerId: string;
  zone: string;
  password: string;
  host?: string;
  port?: number;
  insecure?: boolean;
}): ProxyProvider<ProxyEndpoint>;
```

### `decodo`

Decodo, formerly Smartproxy (https://help.decodo.com/docs/residential-proxy-parameters).
`user-USER-country-us-session-…-sessionduration-10` on gate.decodo.com:7000.

```ts
function decodo(options: {
  username: string;
  password: string;
  host?: string;
  port?: number;
  /** Sticky session lifetime, minutes (1–1440). Default 10. */
  sessionMinutes?: number;
}): ProxyProvider<ProxyEndpoint>;
```

### `smartproxy`

@deprecated Smartproxy is now Decodo.

```ts
const smartproxy: typeof decodo;
```

### `iproyal`

IPRoyal residential (https://docs.iproyal.com/proxies/residential/proxy).
Targeting goes in the password: `PASS_country-us_session-XXXXXXXX_lifetime-10m`.

```ts
function iproyal(options: {
  username: string;
  password: string;
  host?: string;
  port?: number;
  /** Sticky session lifetime, e.g. `10m`, `1h`. Default `10m`. */
  lifetime?: string;
}): ProxyProvider<ProxyEndpoint>;
```

### `nodeMaven`

NodeMaven (https://docs.nodemaven.com): `USER-country-us-sid-…-ttl-10m` on gate.nodemaven.com:8080.
`type` picks the pool (`residential` / `mobile`), `filter` the IP quality.

```ts
function nodeMaven(options: Credentials & {
  type?: "residential" | "mobile";
  filter?: "low" | "medium" | "high";
  ttl?: string;
}): ProxyProvider<ProxyEndpoint>;
```

### `soax`

SOAX (https://helpcenter.soax.com): user `package-ID-country-us-sessionid-…-sessionlength-600`, password = package key.

```ts
function soax(options: {
  packageId: string;
  packageKey: string;
  sessionSeconds?: number;
  host?: string;
  port?: number;
}): ProxyProvider<ProxyEndpoint>;
```

### `netNut`

NetNut (https://help.netnut.io): `USER-res-us-sid-123456789` on gw.netnut.net:5959. Verify for non-residential plans.

```ts
function netNut(options: Credentials): ProxyProvider<ProxyEndpoint>;
```

### `webshare`

Webshare rotating residential (https://apidocs.webshare.io/proxy-connection):
`USER-us-1234` (numeric sticky session) on p.webshare.io:80. `sticky: false` uses `-rotate`
(a new IP per request).

```ts
function webshare(options: Credentials & {
  sticky?: boolean;
}): ProxyProvider<ProxyEndpoint>;
```

### `rayobyte`

Rayobyte (https://docs.rayobyte.com): targeting in the password, `PASS-country-US-session-…-duration-10`.

```ts
function rayobyte(options: Credentials & {
  durationMinutes?: number;
}): ProxyProvider<ProxyEndpoint>;
```

### `packetStream`

PacketStream (https://packetstream.io/docs): password `KEY_country-US_session-…` on proxy.packetstream.io:31112.

```ts
function packetStream(options: Credentials): ProxyProvider<ProxyEndpoint>;
```

### `evomi`

Evomi (https://docs.evomi.com): password `PASS_country-US_session-…_lifetime-30` on rp.evomi.com:1000.

```ts
function evomi(options: Credentials & {
  lifetimeMinutes?: number;
}): ProxyProvider<ProxyEndpoint>;
```

### `dataImpulse`
