### `PROVIDER_NAMES`

Names accepted by `XYTE_PROVIDER`.

```ts
const PROVIDER_NAMES: readonly string[];
```

### `ProxyProvider`

Picks the exit for each attempt. Presets resolve to a `ProxyEndpoint`; API adapters to an `ApiEndpoint`.

```ts
interface ProxyProvider<E extends ProxyEndpoint | ApiEndpoint = ProxyEndpoint | ApiEndpoint> {
  readonly name: string;
  /**
   * The provider answers AI extraction fields itself (Zyte API): requests for them are not
   * rejected upfront for lack of a local extractor.
   */
  readonly extracts?: boolean;
  /**
   * The provider runs Zyte's own actions itself (`searchKeyword`, `setLocation`, `interaction`):
   * with `unsupportedActions: 'error'`, requests using them aren't rejected upfront, and attempts
   * can be passed over to reach it (docs/actions.md).
   */
  readonly zyteActions?: boolean;
  /** The proxy (or API) for this attempt, or null to connect directly. */
  resolve(context: ProxyContext): E | null | Promise<E | null>;
  /**
   * False while the provider shouldn't be used (an open circuit, a spent budget): combinators
   * skip it. Omitted means always available.
   */
  available?(context: ProxyContext): boolean;
  /** How an attempt this provider resolved went. Combinators forward it to the child they chose. */
  report?(context: ProxyContext, outcome: AttemptOutcome): void;
}
```

### `ProxyEndpoint`

A proxy for one attempt: what a proxy provider's `resolve()` returns.

```ts
interface ProxyEndpoint {
  /** `http://user:pass@host:port` (or `https://`). */
  url: string;
  /**
   * Skip TLS verification of the target. Scraping APIs in proxy mode (ZenRows, ScrapingBee,
   * ScraperAPI) re-sign traffic with their own certificate, so it is required for them.
   */
  insecure?: boolean;
  /**
   * Headers added to every request through this proxy, for scraping APIs that take their
   * parameters as headers in proxy mode (Crawlbase, Zyte, Oxylabs Web Unblocker).
   */
  headers?: Record<string, string>;
  /**
   * Reads what a scraping API in proxy mode adds to its answers (HTTP requests only): the final
   * URL after redirects it followed itself, and its own error answers, which are retried as a
   * provider failure instead of being returned as the target's status.
   */
  inspect?: (res: {
    status: number;
    headers: Headers;
  }) => {
    url?: string;
    failure?: string;
  } | undefined;
  /** The provider's bookkeeping headers, left out of `httpResponseHeaders`. */
  hiddenHeaders?: RegExp;
  /**
   * False when this exit ignores the request's `geolocation` (a fixed proxy URL). Such requests
   * still run, with a warning (`onWarning`, `X-Xyte-Warning`).
   */
  appliesCountry?: boolean;
}
```

### `ApiEndpoint`

A scraping service with no proxy port (Scrappey, ScrapingBot, Zyte API itself): it takes the
whole Zyte request and returns a Zyte-shaped response. Ban detection, retries, `rotate()` and
extractors work on its answer as on a proxied download.

```ts
interface ApiEndpoint {
  api: (request: ExtractRequest, info: {
    context: ProxyContext;
    signal: AbortSignal;
  }) => Promise<ApiResult>;
  /**
   * What `request` asks for that this service can't do (e.g. `['actions', 'screenshot']` for an
   * API that only returns a page's HTML). Inside a combinator the attempt is passed over for a
   * provider that can; alone, actions follow `unsupportedActions` and missing outputs are a 400.
   * Omitted: it can do everything.
   */
  unsupported?: (request: ExtractRequest) => readonly string[];
}
```

### `ApiResult`

What an `ApiEndpoint`'s `api()` resolves with: the service's answer in Zyte's shape.

```ts
interface ApiResult {
  /** The Zyte-shaped response (url, statusCode, httpResponseBody / browserHtml, …). */
  response: ExtractResponse;
  /** The target's status, for ban detection. */
  statusCode: number;
  headers?: {
    name: string;
    value: string;
  }[];
  /** The page as text, for ban detection and extractors. */
  html?: string;
  /** The service already handled bans (Zyte): skip xyte's ban check on this answer. */
  trusted?: boolean;
}
```

### `ProxyContext`

What a provider gets to pick an exit for one attempt of one request.

```ts
interface ProxyContext {
  /** Target URL. */
  url: URL;
  /** ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, upper case, from the request's `geolocation`. */
  country?: string;
  /** From the request's `ipType`. */
  ipType?: "datacenter" | "residential";
  /**
   * Sticky-session key: the request's `session.id`, or a fresh id per attempt. Providers map it
   * to their session parameter so every hop of one attempt (redirects, browser sub-requests)
   * leaves from one IP, and a retry leaves from another.
   */
  sessionId: string;
  /** 0 for the first try, then 1, 2… */
  attempt: number;
  /** The attempt renders in a browser (every page sub-request goes through the proxy). */
  browser: boolean;
  /** Unique per `extract()` call: combinators use it to tell attempts of one request apart. */
  requestId?: string;
  /** Providers chosen so far by combinators, outermost first; the last is the one that served. */
  path?: string[];
}
```

### `EndpointOf`

The endpoint type a provider resolves to.

```ts
type EndpointOf<P> = P extends ProxyProvider<infer E> ? E : never;
```

### `AttemptOutcome`

How an attempt went, reported to the provider that served it (and to `onAttempt`).

```ts
interface AttemptOutcome {
  /**
   * `ok`: the page came back (a target's own 404 included). `ban`: a ban or challenge page.
   * `error`: the proxy or network failed. `aborted`: no verdict on the provider (an invalid
   * request, a cancelled call, another attempt's failure).
   */
  result: "ok" | "ban" | "error" | "aborted";
  /** Milliseconds the attempt took. */
  ms: number;
  statusCode?: number;
  /** Size of the page that came back (decoded body or browser HTML). */
  bytes?: number;
  /**
   * Bytes that crossed the wire, both ways: headers, compressed bodies, redirects and, in a
   * browser, every sub-request. What a per-GB proxy bills, minus TLS/tunnel overhead.
   */
  transferBytes?: number;
  reason?: string;
  /** Captchas met in a browser render with `browser.captcha`, and whether they were solved. */
  captchas?: {
    kind: string;
    solver: string;
    solved: boolean;
    ms: number;
    error?: string;
  }[];
}
```

## Combining providers

Providers built from other providers. [Routing](routing.md) explains each, with examples.

### `rotate`

Tries providers in order across attempts: attempt 0 → first, attempt 1 → second… and wraps.
A provider outage (e.g. a 407 on every request) then costs one attempt, not the request.
Unavailable providers (an open `healthy()` circuit, a spent `budget()`) are skipped.

```ts
function rotate<P extends ProxyProvider>(providers: readonly P[]): ProxyProvider<EndpointOf<P>>;
```

### `route`

Picks the provider by the target's host, so each site gets the cheapest exit that works on it:
`route({ 'doordash.com': zyteApi(…), 'wolt.com': direct() }, residential)`. A key matches the
host and its subdomains (`doordash.com` matches `www.doordash.com`); the longest match wins.
Every attempt of a request, retries included, stays on its route: nest `rotate()` inside a
route for a fallback.

```ts
function route<R extends Readonly<Record<string, ProxyProvider>>, F extends ProxyProvider>(routes: R, fallback: F): ProxyProvider<EndpointOf<R[keyof R] | F>>;
```

### `adaptive`

Learns, per site, the cheapest provider that works. List providers cheapest first:
`adaptive([direct(), residential, zyteApi(…)])`. Each request starts at the first provider
whose success score on that site is at least `minSuccess`; a retry moves to the next one.
Scores start optimistic and follow outcomes (bans and errors lower them), and a small share of
requests re-tests the cheaper ones, so a site that stops blocking moves back down.

```ts
function adaptive<P extends ProxyProvider>(providers: readonly P[], options?: AdaptiveOptions): AdaptiveProvider<EndpointOf<P>>;
```

### `byKind`

One provider for plain HTTP requests, another for browser renders. Scraping APIs bill every
sub-request of a render, residential proxies bill per GB: `byKind({ http: scrapingBee(…),
browser: oxylabs(…) })`.

```ts
function byKind<H extends ProxyProvider, B extends ProxyProvider>(providers: {
  http: H;
  browser: B;
}): ProxyProvider<EndpointOf<H | B>>;
```

### `byCountry`

Picks the provider by the request's `geolocation` (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2): some networks are
better, or cheaper, in some countries. `byCountry({ US: oxylabs(…), FI: direct() }, decodo(…))`.

```ts
function byCountry<R extends Readonly<Record<string, ProxyProvider>>, F extends ProxyProvider>(countries: R, fallback: F): ProxyProvider<EndpointOf<R[keyof R] | F>>;
```

### `byIpType`

Uses `datacenter` or `residential` per the request's `ipType`.

```ts
function byIpType<D extends ProxyProvider = never, R extends ProxyProvider = never>(providers: {
  datacenter?: D;
  residential?: R;
  /** When the request sets no `ipType`. Default: `datacenter` if given, else `residential`. */
  default?: "datacenter" | "residential";
}): ProxyProvider<EndpointOf<D | R>>;
```

### `weighted`

Splits traffic by weight, e.g. to try a new provider on 10% of requests:
`weighted([[current, 9], [candidate, 1]])`. Each request picks once (by its id); its retries
move on to the next provider, skipping unavailable ones.

```ts
function weighted<P extends ProxyProvider>(entries: readonly (readonly [P, number])[]): ProxyProvider<EndpointOf<P>>;
```

### `healthy`

A circuit breaker: after `failures` consecutive proxy/network errors (a 407 on every login, a
gateway outage), the provider is reported unavailable for `cooldown` seconds, and `rotate()`,
`weighted()` and `adaptive()` go straight to the others instead of losing an attempt on it.
Bans don't count: they say the site blocked an IP, not that the provider is down. Used alone,
an open circuit doesn't block requests (there is nothing to fall back to).

```ts
function healthy<P extends ProxyProvider>(provider: P, options?: HealthyOptions): ProxyProvider<EndpointOf<P>>;
```

### `budget`

Caps how many attempts go to a provider per time window, e.g. so a fallback to Zyte can't
run up the bill when a site starts blocking the cheaper exits: `rotate([residential,
budget(zyteApi(…), { max: 500, per: 'hour' })])`. Attempts that failed at the network level
are given back. Once spent, `rotate()` and the others skip it; used alone (or when every
option is spent), requests fail with a 429 `/limits/over-user-limit`, retryable later.

```ts
function budget<P extends ProxyProvider>(provider: P, options: BudgetOptions): ProxyProvider<EndpointOf<P>>;
```

### `watch`

Asks a provider how it is, ahead of requests: its usage API (credits left) or status page. An
exhausted or down provider is reported unavailable, so `rotate()`, `route()`, `weighted()` and
`adaptive()` skip it before an attempt is wasted on it. Checks run in the background every
`every` seconds, never on the request path; until the first one answers, the provider counts as
available. Used alone, an unavailable provider is still used (there is nothing to fall back to).

```ts
function watch<P extends ProxyProvider>(provider: P, options: WatchOptions): WatchedProvider<EndpointOf<P>>;
```

### `AdaptiveOptions`

Options of `adaptive()`.

```ts
interface AdaptiveOptions {
  /** A provider is used for a site while its success score there is at least this. Default 0.5. */
  minSuccess?: number;
  /** Share of requests that re-test a cheaper provider the site had stopped working on. Default 0.05. */
  explore?: number;
  /** How fast scores follow recent outcomes, 0–1. Default 0.2. */
  learningRate?: number;
  /** The key scores are kept by. Default: the host without `www.`. */
  keyOf?: (url: URL) => string;
  /**
   * Shared state: every instance learns from every other's outcomes. Updates go to the store as
   * they happen; each instance re-reads a site's scores in the background every `syncEvery`
   * seconds. Default: this process only.
   */
  store?: StateStore;
  /** The scores' key prefix in the store. Default: the adaptive provider's name. */
  key?: string;
  /** Seconds between background re-reads of a site's shared scores. Default 5. */
  syncEvery?: number;
}
```

### `AdaptiveProvider`

What `adaptive()` returns: a provider that also reports its learned scores.

```ts
type AdaptiveProvider<E extends ProxyEndpoint | ApiEndpoint> = ProxyProvider<E> & {
  /** Current scores, by site and provider (1: always works, 0: never). */
  scores(): Record<string, Record<string, number>>;
};
```

### `HealthyOptions`

Options of `healthy()`, the circuit breaker.

```ts
interface HealthyOptions {
  /** Consecutive failed attempts (proxy or network errors, not bans) that open the circuit. Default 5. */
  failures?: number;
  /** Seconds the circuit stays open. Then one attempt is let through: a failure reopens it. Default 60. */
  cooldown?: number;
  /** Called when the circuit opens (`true`) or closes again (`false`). */
  onChange?: (open: boolean, provider: string) => void;
  /** Shared state: a circuit one instance opens is open for all of them. Default: this process only. */
  store?: StateStore;
  /** The circuit's key in the store. Default: the provider's name. */
  key?: string;
}
```

### `BudgetOptions`

Options of `budget()`.

```ts
interface BudgetOptions {
  /** Attempts allowed per window. */
  max: number;
  /** The window: seconds, or `minute`, `hour`, `day`. Windows are fixed (they start on the clock). */
  per: number | "minute" | "hour" | "day";
  /** Shared state: every instance spends from one budget. Default: this process only. */
  store?: StateStore;
  /** The budget's key in the store. Default: the provider's name. */
  key?: string;
}
```

### `WatchOptions`

Options of `watch()`.

```ts
interface WatchOptions {
  /** One or more checks; the provider is available while all of them say so. */
  check: ProviderCheck | readonly ProviderCheck[];
  /** Seconds between checks. Default 60. */
  every?: number;
  /** Seconds a check may take. Default 10. */
  timeout?: number;
  /** Shared state: one instance checks, the others reuse its answer until it's `every` old. */
  store?: StateStore;
  /** The result's key in the store. Default: the provider's name. */
  key?: string;
  /** Called when availability changes (and on a first result that is unavailable). */
  onChange?: (result: CheckResult, provider: string) => void;
  /** Called when a check itself fails; the last result stays in place. */
  onError?: (error: unknown, provider: string) => void;
}
```

### `WatchedProvider`

What `watch()` returns: a provider that also exposes its last check.

```ts
type WatchedProvider<E extends ProxyEndpoint | ApiEndpoint> = ProxyProvider<E> & {
  /** The last check's result; undefined before the first one finished. */
  status(): CheckResult | undefined;
  /** Checks now (e.g. at startup, to know before the first request) and resolves with the result. */
  refresh(): Promise<CheckResult | undefined>;
};
```

## Provider checks

Checks for `watch()`: [routing](routing.md#watch-check-providers-ahead-of-requests).

### `scrapingBeeUsage`

ScrapingBee credits: unavailable once fewer than `minRemaining` are left (default 0).
Uses `GET app.scrapingbee.com/api/v1/usage` (checked against a live account).

```ts
function scrapingBeeUsage(options: CheckOptions & {
  apiKey: string;
  minRemaining?: number;
}): ProviderCheck;
```

### `zenrowsUsage`

ZenRows plan usage: unavailable when the subscription isn't active, its usage reaches
`maxPercent` (default 100), or the key's own credit caps are spent.
Uses `GET api.zenrows.com/v1/subscriptions/self/details` (from ZenRows's docs).

```ts
function zenrowsUsage(options: CheckOptions & {
  apiKey: string;
  maxPercent?: number;
}): ProviderCheck;
```

### `scraperApiUsage`

ScraperAPI requests: unavailable once `requestCount` reaches `requestLimit`.
Uses `GET api.scraperapi.com/account` (from ScraperAPI's docs; not checked against an account).

```ts
function scraperApiUsage(options: CheckOptions & {
  apiKey: string;
}): ProviderCheck;
```

### `oxylabsUsage`

Oxylabs residential traffic this month, against your plan's `limitGB` (the API reports usage,
not the limit): unavailable from `maxPercent` of it (default 100). Logs in to
`residential-api.oxylabs.io/v2` with the account's *main* proxy user (the first in the
dashboard), which may differ from the user requests go out with. From Oxylabs's docs; not yet
checked against an account.

```ts
function oxylabsUsage(options: CheckOptions & {
  username: string;
  password: string;
  limitGB: number;
  maxPercent?: number;
}): ProviderCheck;
```

### `statusPage`

A Statuspage page (`https://status.zyte.com`, IPRoyal, Webshare…): unavailable while its
indicator is one of `downOn` (default `major`, `critical`; `minor` is a partial degradation).

```ts
function statusPage(url: string, options?: CheckOptions & {
  downOn?: readonly string[];
}): ProviderCheck;
```

### `STATUS_PAGES`

Status pages known for providers xyte has presets for.

```ts
const STATUS_PAGES: Readonly<Record<string, string>>;
```

### `ProviderCheck`

Asks a provider's API or status page how it is. Built-in ones are in `checks`.

```ts
type ProviderCheck = (signal: AbortSignal) => Promise<CheckResult>;
```

### `CheckResult`

What a provider check found: whether to use the provider, and why.

```ts
interface CheckResult {
  available: boolean;
  /** Human-readable state, e.g. `820/1000 credits used`. */
  detail?: string;
  /** What's left, in the check's own unit (credits, requests, GB), when it knows. */
  remaining?: number;
}
```

## Shared state

Where budgets, circuits, checks, `adaptive`, sessions, the cache, jobs and stats keep their state: [routing](routing.md#shared-state-across-instances-redis), [lifecycle](lifecycle.md) for closing a Redis store.

### `StateStore`

Where `budget()`, `healthy()` and `watch()` keep their state. In memory (the default) each
process counts on its own; with a shared store (Redis) every instance of a deployment sees the
same budget, the same open circuits and the same provider checks.

```ts
interface StateStore {
  /** Adds `by` (negative to give back) to a counter that expires `ttl` seconds after it's created. */
  incr(key: string, by: number, ttl: number): Promise<number>;
  get(key: string): Promise<string | null>;
  set(key: string, value: string, ttl: number): Promise<void>;
  /**
   * Releases what the store holds open, such as a Redis connection (which, with some clients, keeps
   * the process from exiting). Optional: memory stores and `redisStore(send)` have nothing to close.
   */
  close?(): Promise<void>;
}
```

### `memoryStore`

State in this process. `maxEntries` caps it, dropping the least recently written first.

```ts
function memoryStore(options?: {
  maxEntries?: number;
}): StateStore;
```

### `redisStore`

State in Redis, through any client: pass how to send a raw command.

```ts
redisStore((c) => bunRedis.send(c[0]!, c.slice(1)));   // Bun.redis / new Bun.RedisClient(url)
redisStore((c) => ioredis.call(c[0]!, ...c.slice(1))); // ioredis
redisStore((c) => nodeRedis.sendCommand(c));           // node-redis
```

Or `redisStoreFromUrl(url)`, which picks one of those.

```ts
function redisStore(send: RedisSend, options?: {
  prefix?: string;
}): StateStore;
```

### `redisStoreFromUrl`

Redis at `url` (`redis://…`) with the client at hand: Bun's built-in one, else the `ioredis` or
`redis` package if installed. The connection opens on first use; `close()` (or `await using`)
closes it, which on Node with `ioredis` or `redis` is what lets the process exit.

```ts
function redisStoreFromUrl(url: string, options?: {
  prefix?: string;
}): StateStore & {
  close(): Promise<void>;
} & AsyncDisposable;
```

### `resilient`

A store that never fails a request: when the shared store errors (Redis down), the operation
falls back to process memory and `onError` hears about it once per outage.

```ts
function resilient(store: StateStore, onError?: (error: unknown) => void): StateStore;
```

### `RedisSend`

Sends one Redis command, e.g. `['INCRBY', 'key', '1']`, and resolves with its reply.

```ts
type RedisSend = (command: string[]) => Promise<unknown>;
```

## Actions

Zyte's own actions outside Zyte: [actions](actions.md).

### `ActionHandlers`

The `actions` option: how `searchKeyword`, `setLocation` and `interaction` run outside Zyte.
Each takes a handler, or a table by site (`PerSite`) or by id (`ById`). See docs/actions.md.

```ts
interface ActionHandlers {
  /** `'*'` defaults to `searchBox`, a heuristic that finds the page's search box; `null` (or `false`) turns it off. */
  searchKeyword?: PerSite<SearchKeywordAction> | false;
  /** `'*'` defaults to none: forms to set a location are different on every site. */
  setLocation?: PerSite<SetLocationAction>;
  /** Your scripts by id; `'*'` defaults to none. */
  interaction?: ById<InteractionAction>;
}
```

### `ActionHandler`

Runs one action on the page; throw to fail it (its `onError` then applies, as for any action).

```ts
type ActionHandler<A extends ZyteOnlyAction> = (page: Page, action: A, context: ActionHandlerContext) => Promise<void>;
```

### `ActionHandlerContext`

What an action handler gets besides the page and the action.

```ts
interface ActionHandlerContext {
  /** The page's current URL. */
  url: URL;
  /** Milliseconds the action may take: 30 s, within the browser time left (these actions have no `timeout` of their own). */
  timeout: number;
  /** Adds a line to the action's `interactionLogs` in the response, as Zyte does with its scripts' `console.log`. */
  log: (message: string, level?: "debug" | "info" | "warning" | "error") => void;
}
```

### `ActionEntry`

A handler, or `null` for explicitly none (no fallback, no built-in).

```ts
type ActionEntry<A extends ZyteOnlyAction> = ActionHandler<A> | null;
```

### `PerSite`

Handlers by site: keys are hosts (subdomains included, the longest key wins), `'*'` is every
other site. A plain function is the same as `{ '*': fn }`.

```ts
type PerSite<A extends ZyteOnlyAction> = ActionHandler<A> | Readonly<Record<string, ActionEntry<A>>>;
```

### `ById`

Handlers by the `id` the action names; `'*'` is every other id. A plain function is `{ '*': fn }`.

```ts
type ById<A extends ZyteOnlyAction> = ActionHandler<A> | Readonly<Record<string, ActionEntry<A>>>;
```

### `SearchKeywordAction`

Zyte's `searchKeyword` action: type `keyword` into the page's search box and submit.

```ts
type SearchKeywordAction = Extract<Action, {
  action: "searchKeyword";
}>;
```

### `SetLocationAction`

Zyte's `setLocation` action: set the site's delivery or store location to an address.

```ts
type SetLocationAction = Extract<Action, {
  action: "setLocation";
}>;
```

### `InteractionAction`

Zyte's `interaction` action: run a script by `id` (on Zyte, one from its cloud IDE).

```ts
type InteractionAction = Extract<Action, {
  action: "interaction";
}>;
```

### `ZyteOnlyAction`

Zyte's own actions, which rely on Zyte's per-site knowledge (`searchKeyword`, `setLocation`) or
on scripts stored in Zyte's cloud IDE (`interaction`). Zyte runs them on attempts that reach
`zyteApi()`; elsewhere they run in xyte's browser through handlers: yours (which always run
locally), or the built-in heuristic for `searchKeyword`. Without one, `unsupportedActions`
decides (skip with a warning, pass over to Zyte, or a 400). See docs/actions.md.

```ts
type ZyteOnlyAction = SearchKeywordAction | SetLocationAction | InteractionAction;
```

### `searchBox`

The default `searchKeyword`: finds the page's search box (search inputs, `role=searchbox`, a
`q`/`query`/`search` field, a "search" placeholder or label; opening a search toggle first when
the box is hidden behind one), types the keyword and presses Enter. Like Zyte's, it fails when
the page has no search box; sites it gets wrong can have their own handler.

```ts
const searchBox: ActionHandler<SearchKeywordAction>;
```

### `isZyteOnlyAction`

Whether an action is one of Zyte's own three (`searchKeyword`, `setLocation`, `interaction`).

```ts
const isZyteOnlyAction: (action: Action) => action is ZyteOnlyAction;
```

## Browser

Renders: launching, stealth presets, remote browsers, captchas. [Browser](browser.md).

### `patchright`

Patchright: Playwright patched against CDP-based detection (Chromium).

```ts
function patchright(): BrowserOptions;
```

### `rebrowser`

rebrowser-playwright: Playwright with the rebrowser patches (Chromium), a drop-in.

```ts
function rebrowser(): BrowserOptions;
```

### `camoufox`

Camoufox: a Firefox build that spoofs its fingerprint at the C++ level, through `camoufox-js`. Options go to `Camoufox()`.

```ts
function camoufox(options?: Record<string, unknown>): BrowserOptions;
```

### `cloakBrowser`

CloakBrowser: a Chromium patched at the source level against fingerprinting. Options go to its `launch()`.

```ts
function cloakBrowser(options?: Record<string, unknown>): BrowserOptions;
```

### `STEALTH_BROWSERS`

The presets by their `XYTE_BROWSER` names.

```ts
const STEALTH_BROWSERS: Readonly<Record<string, () => BrowserOptions>>;
```

### `capsolver`

CapSolver (capsolver.com): reCAPTCHA v2/v3 and Turnstile, without a proxy of its own. From its docs; not checked against an account.

```ts
function capsolver(options: {
  apiKey: string;
  fetch?: typeof fetch;
  timeout?: number;
  pollEvery?: number;
}): CaptchaSolver;
```

### `twoCaptcha`

2Captcha (2captcha.com), API v2: reCAPTCHA v2/v3, hCaptcha and Turnstile. From its docs; not checked against an account.

```ts
function twoCaptcha(options: {
  apiKey: string;
  fetch?: typeof fetch;
  timeout?: number;
  pollEvery?: number;
}): CaptchaSolver;
```

### `createTaskSolver`

A solver for services with the `createTask` / `getTaskResult` API (CapSolver, 2Captcha, and
others that copied it): `types` maps each kind to the service's task type.

```ts
function createTaskSolver(options: {
  name: string;
  endpoint: string;
  apiKey: string;
  types: Partial<Record<CaptchaKind, string>>;
  /** Seconds between result polls. Default 3. */
  pollEvery?: number;
  /** Seconds before giving up. Default 120. */
  timeout?: number;
  fetch?: typeof fetch;
}): CaptchaSolver;
```

### `CaptchaSolver`

Solves captchas for browser renders (`browser.captcha`): `capsolver()`, `twoCaptcha()`, or your own.

```ts
interface CaptchaSolver {
  readonly name: string;
  /** Resolves with the token the widget would have produced. */
  solve(task: CaptchaTask, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<string>;
}
```

### `CaptchaTask`

A captcha found on a page, as a solver gets it.

```ts
interface CaptchaTask {
  kind: CaptchaKind;
  siteKey: string;
  /** The page the widget is on. */
  url: string;
  /** reCAPTCHA v3 / Turnstile `action`, when the widget declares one. */
  action?: string;
}
```

### `CaptchaKind`

Captcha solving in browser renders: after the page loads (before your actions), a reCAPTCHA,
hCaptcha or Cloudflare Turnstile widget on it is sent to a solving service, and its token is put
where the page's form expects it, calling the widget's callback. Cloudflare's full-page "Just a
moment…" challenge is a different mechanism (cookies and fingerprint), not handled here.

```ts
type CaptchaKind = "recaptchaV2" | "recaptchaV3" | "hcaptcha" | "turnstile";
```

### `CaptchaOutcome`

What happened to a captcha found on the page (in the attempt report).

```ts
interface CaptchaOutcome {
  kind: CaptchaKind;
  solver: string;
  solved: boolean;
  ms: number;
  error?: string;
}
```

### `BrowserOptions`

The `browser` option: how renders run. A local Chromium by default; `launch` for your own
(Patchright, Camoufox…: see the stealth presets), `connect` for a hosted browser, plus page
hooks, stealth and captcha solving. See docs/browser.md.

```ts
interface BrowserOptions {
  /**
   * The Playwright-compatible browser type to launch. Default: `chromium` from `playwright`
   * (an optional peer dependency). Swap in a fork for stealth, e.g.
   * `(await import('patchright')).chromium`, `rebrowser-playwright`, or `playwright-extra`
   * with its stealth plugin.
   */
  browserType?: BrowserTypeLike | (() => BrowserTypeLike | Promise<BrowserTypeLike>);
  /** Options for `browserType.launch()`: `headless`, `channel: 'chrome'`, `args`, `executablePath`… */
  launchOptions?: LaunchOptions;
  /** Full control over the shared browser (overrides `browserType` / `launchOptions`). */
  launch?: () => Promise<unknown>;
  /**
   * Render each request in a remote browser instead: Bright Data Scraping Browser, Browserless,
   * Browserbase… Called per attempt with the country and session, so the endpoint can carry
   * them. The connection is closed after the request.
   */
  connect?: (context: ProxyContext) => string | RemoteBrowser | Promise<string | RemoteBrowser>;
  /**
   * Adjust the context options per request. Receives xyte's defaults (proxy, viewport, user
   * agent, locale…); return the options to use. Patchright, for instance, recommends dropping
   * the custom `userAgent` and `viewport`.
   */
  contextOptions?: (defaults: BrowserContextOptions, info: BrowserHookInfo) => BrowserContextOptions | Promise<BrowserContextOptions>;
  /** Runs on every new page before navigation: init scripts, routes, stealth patches. */
  onPage?: (page: Page, info: BrowserHookInfo) => void | Promise<void>;
  /**
   * Resource types to abort, to save proxy bandwidth (residential traffic is billed per GB),
   * e.g. `['image', 'media', 'font']`.
   */
  blockResources?: readonly string[];
  /** Total browser time per request, seconds. Zyte's limit is 60. */
  timeLimit?: number;
  /**
   * Solves reCAPTCHA, hCaptcha and Turnstile widgets found after the page loads, before the
   * actions: `capsolver({ apiKey })`, `twoCaptcha({ apiKey })`, or your own `CaptchaSolver`.
   */
  captcha?: CaptchaSolver;
  /**
   * After load and the actions, wait up to this many seconds for the network to go quiet, so
   * data the page fetches after `load` lands in `browserHtml` and `networkCapture`, as on Zyte.
   * Default 3; 0 returns right after load.
   */
  settleTime?: number;
}
```

### `BrowserHookInfo`

What hooks get to see about the request being rendered.

```ts
interface BrowserHookInfo {
  request: EngineAttempt["request"];
  proxy: ProxyEndpoint | null;
  context: ProxyContext;
}
```

### `BrowserTypeLike`

The part of a Playwright `BrowserType` xyte uses. Typed loosely on purpose: forks (patchright,
rebrowser-playwright…) declare their own, nominally different, Browser types.

```ts
interface BrowserTypeLike {
  launch(options?: any): Promise<unknown>;
  connect(wsEndpoint: string, options?: any): Promise<unknown>;
  connectOverCDP(endpointURL: string, options?: any): Promise<unknown>;
}
```

### `RemoteBrowser`

A remote browser to render one request in.

```ts
interface RemoteBrowser {
  /** `wss://…` (or `http://…` for CDP discovery). */
  endpoint: string;
  /** `cdp` (default) for `connectOverCDP`, `playwright` for a Playwright server (`connect`). */
  protocol?: "cdp" | "playwright";
  headers?: Record<string, string>;
  /**
   * Also route the browser through xyte's `proxy`. Default false: remote browser services
   * pick their own exit (set the country in the endpoint).
   */
  useProxy?: boolean;
}
```

## Extraction

AI extraction fields and Markdown: [extraction](extraction.md).

### `Extractor`

Computes one AI-extraction output (e.g. `product`) from the downloaded page.

```ts
type Extractor = (input: {
  url: string;
  html: string;
  request: ExtractRequest;
  /** Options of the field, e.g. `productOptions`. */
  options: unknown;
}) => unknown | Promise<unknown>;
```

### `llmExtractors`

Extractors for `new Xyte({ extractors: llmExtractors({ complete }) })`. Each runs one model
call per requested field.

```ts
function llmExtractors(options: LlmExtractorOptions): Partial<Record<ExtractionField, Extractor>>;
```

### `openAICompatible`

`complete` for any OpenAI-compatible chat completions API:

    openAICompatible({ baseURL: 'https://openrouter.ai/api/v1', apiKey, model: 'openai/gpt-5-mini' })
    openAICompatible({ baseURL: 'http://localhost:11434/v1', model: 'qwen3' })   // Ollama

```ts
function openAICompatible(options: {
  model: string;
  apiKey?: string;
  /** Default `https://api.openai.com/v1`. */
  baseURL?: string;
  headers?: Record<string, string>;
  temperature?: number;
  /** Ask for `response_format: json_schema` (default) or plain `json_object` for servers without it. */
  responseFormat?: "json_schema" | "json_object";
  fetch?: typeof fetch;
}): Complete;
```

### `Complete`

Calls your model: gets a `CompletionRequest`, returns the answer (text, an object, or a `Completion`).
`openAICompatible()` makes one for any OpenAI-compatible API.

```ts
type Complete = (request: CompletionRequest) => Promise<string | object | Completion>;
```

### `CompletionRequest`

One model call `llmExtractors()` makes: a prompt for one extraction field, and the schema to answer in.

```ts
interface CompletionRequest {
  /** The extraction field, e.g. `product`. */
  field: ExtractionField;
  system: string;
  prompt: string;
  /** JSON Schema the answer must match. */
  schema: object;
}
```

### `Completion`

A model's answer, with its token usage if known.

```ts
interface Completion {
  /** The model's answer: JSON text (code fences are tolerated) or an already-parsed object. */
  output: string | object;
  usage?: {
    inputTokens?: number;
    outputTokens?: number;
  };
}
```

### `LlmExtractorOptions`

Options of `llmExtractors()`.

```ts
interface LlmExtractorOptions {
  complete: Complete;
  /** Fields to provide. Default: all AI fields (product…pageContent, serp, customAttributes). */
  fields?: readonly ExtractionField[];
  /** Page text sent to the model, in characters (~4 per token). Default 60 000. */
  maxInputChars?: number;
}
```

### `parseJson`

Parses a model answer, tolerating ```json fences and text around the object.

```ts
function parseJson(output: string | object): Record<string, unknown>;
```

### `htmlToMarkdown`

The built-in `markdown` extraction: HTML to Markdown, the main content only (Zyte's default) or the
whole page. Relative links and images are resolved against `url`.

```ts
function htmlToMarkdown(html: string, options?: MarkdownOptions): string;
```

### `MarkdownOptions`

Options of `htmlToMarkdown()`.

```ts
interface MarkdownOptions {
  /** Base for relative links and images. */
  url?: string;
  /** Zyte's `markdownOptions.scope`. Default `mainContent`. */
  scope?: "mainContent" | "fullPage";
}
```

### `OUTPUT_SCHEMAS`

Zyte's JSON Schema for each AI extraction field (`product`, `article`…), as `llmExtractors()` asks models to answer in.

```ts
const OUTPUT_SCHEMAS: Record<OutputSchemaField, object>;
```

### `OutputSchemaField`

The extraction fields with an output schema.

```ts
type OutputSchemaField = "product" | "productList" | "productNavigation" | "article" | "articleList" | "articleNavigation" | "forumThread" | "jobPosting" | "jobPostingNavigation" | "pageContent" | "serp";
```

## Reports, costs, cache and pacing

What each request took and cost: [observability](observability.md); the cache and rate limits: [configuration](configuration.md).

### `RequestReport`

What one `extract()` took and how it ended: `onRequest` / `onReport`.

```ts
interface RequestReport {
  requestId: string;
  url: string;
  host: string;
  /** The request's `tags` (Zyte's way to label requests for its stats), for grouping reports. */
  tags?: ExtractRequest["tags"];
  /** The request's `jobId`, if it had one. */
  jobId?: string;
  /** `ok`: a response came back (the target's own 4xx/5xx included); `error`: an `XyteError`; `aborted`: cancelled. */
  outcome: "ok" | "error" | "aborted";
  /** The target's status, when a response came back. */
  statusCode?: number;
  /** The problem it failed with. */
  error?: XyteProblem;
  /** The provider that served the response (the last attempt's). */
  provider?: string;
  /** The last attempt rendered in a browser. */
  browser: boolean;
  /** `browserFallback` moved it from HTTP to a browser. */
  escalated: boolean;
  /** Milliseconds waiting for a `concurrency` slot, then working. */
  queuedMs: number;
  /**
   * With `cache`: `hit` (answered from the cache: no attempts), `shared` (an identical request
   * in flight answered it), or `miss` (fetched, and stored if cacheable).
   */
  cache?: "hit" | "shared" | "miss";
  ms: number;
  attempts: AttemptInfo[];
  /** Totals over the attempts. */
  transferBytes: number;
  /** With `rates`: what the request cost, in USD (0 for a cache hit). */
  costUsd?: number;
  byProvider: Record<string, ProviderUsage>;
  warnings: string[];
}
```

### `AttemptInfo`

One attempt of an `extract()`: which provider, how it went, how long, how many bytes, what it cost.
Passed to `onAttempt`, and listed in `RequestReport.attempts`.

```ts
interface AttemptInfo extends AttemptOutcome {
  /** The `extract()` call it belongs to (same id as its `RequestReport`). */
  requestId: string;
  url: string;
  /** 0 for the first try. */
  attempt: number;
  /** The combinators' choices down to `provider`, outermost first, e.g. `['rotate(oxylabs-residential,zyte-api)', 'zyte-api']`. */
  path: string[];
  /** The provider that served the attempt: the leaf a combinator chose, e.g. `oxylabs-residential`. */
  provider: string;
  /** Rendered in a browser (requested, or `browserFallback`). */
  browser: boolean;
  /** The request's `tags` (as on Zyte, e.g. `{ spider: 'yelp' }`), to group attempts by in metrics. */
  tags?: ExtractRequest["tags"];
  /** With `rates`: what this attempt cost, in USD. */
  costUsd?: number;
}
```

### `ProviderUsage`

Attempts and bytes of one provider within a request (or across reports, summed).

```ts
interface ProviderUsage {
  attempts: number;
  ok: number;
  ban: number;
  error: number;
  aborted: number;
  /** Bytes on the wire (`transferBytes`), summed. */
  transferBytes: number;
  /** Time spent in its attempts, summed. */
  ms: number;
  /** With `rates`: what its attempts cost, in USD. */
  costUsd?: number;
}
```

### `usageByProvider`

Sums attempts per provider.

```ts
function usageByProvider(attempts: readonly AttemptInfo[]): Record<string, ProviderUsage>;
```

### `Rate`

What a provider costs you. All in USD; any combination.

```ts
interface Rate {
  /** Per GB on the wire (`transferBytes`): residential and datacenter proxies. */
  perGB?: number;
  /** Per attempt that got an answer (`ok` or `ban`): APIs that bill every request. */
  perRequest?: number;
  /** Per `ok` attempt only: APIs that bill successful requests. */
  perSuccess?: number;
}
```

### `Rates`

Your prices by provider name (`oxylabs`, `zyte-api`…); a name also covers its variants (`oxylabs` → `oxylabs-residential`).

```ts
type Rates = Readonly<Record<string, Rate>>;
```

### `rateFor`

The rate for a provider: its exact name, else the longest key it starts with (`oxylabs` → `oxylabs-residential`).

```ts
function rateFor(rates: Rates, provider: string): Rate | undefined;
```

### `attemptCost`

What one attempt cost at `rate`. Errors and pass-overs got no answer: nothing to bill.

```ts
function attemptCost(rate: Rate | undefined, attempt: Pick<AttemptOutcome, "result" | "transferBytes">): number;
```

### `CacheOptions`

The `cache` option: keep responses for a while and answer repeated requests from them.

```ts
interface CacheOptions {
  /**
   * Seconds a response stays fresh: one value for every site, or per site keyed by host
   * (subdomains included, the longest key wins) with `'*'` for the rest. 0 doesn't cache.
   */
  ttl: number | Readonly<Record<string, number>>;
  /** Where responses are kept. Default: this process's memory (1,000 responses). Redis shares them across instances. */
  store?: StateStore;
  /** Which responses to keep. Default: the target answered below 400, or 404 / 410 (gone stays gone). */
  cacheable?: (response: ExtractResponse) => boolean;
  /** The cache key. Default: a hash of the request without `tags`, `jobId` and `echoData`, which don't change the page. */
  key?: (request: ExtractRequest) => string;
}
```

### `requestKey`

The cache's default key: a hash of the request without its labels (`tags`, `jobId`, `echoData`),
so the same request with different tags is a hit.

```ts
function requestKey(request: ExtractRequest): string;
```

### `RateLimits`

Keyed by host (subdomains included, the longest key wins), `'*'` for every other site, each on
its own (`'*': '10/s'` is 10 per second per site). Values: `'2/s'`, `'120/m'`, `'1000/h'`,
`'5/10s'`, or a `SiteLimit`.

```ts
type RateLimits = Readonly<Record<string, string | SiteLimit>>;
```

### `SiteLimit`

`rate` attempts per `per` seconds, at most `concurrency` at once.

```ts
interface SiteLimit {
  rate?: number;
  /** Seconds. Default 1. */
  per?: number;
  concurrency?: number;
}
```

### `parseLimit`

Parses a rate limit like `'2/s'`, `'120/m'` or `'5/10s'` into `{ rate, per }` (`per` in seconds).

```ts
function parseLimit(value: string | SiteLimit): SiteLimit;
```

## Server

Serving Zyte's APIs: [deploy](deploy.md), [mounting](mounting.md), [proxy mode](proxy-mode.md).

### `createHandler`

A Web-standard handler serving Zyte's HTTP API: `POST /v1/extract`. Mount it with `Bun.serve`,
Deno, Hono, a Cloudflare Worker… then point existing Zyte code at it by changing only the base
URL (`https://api.zyte.com/v1/extract` → `http://localhost:8011/v1/extract`).

```ts
function createHandler(xyte: Xyte, options?: HandlerOptions): FetchHandler;
```

### `HandlerOptions`

Options of `createHandler()`.

```ts
interface HandlerOptions {
  /**
   * Accepted API keys, sent like Zyte's: HTTP basic auth with the key as the username. When
   * empty or omitted, any (or no) key is accepted.
   */
  apiKeys?: readonly string[];
  /**
   * Where the routes live, e.g. `/zyte` for `/zyte/v1/extract`. Default: any path ending in
   * `/v1/extract` (or `/healthz`), so the handler works mounted under a prefix whether or not the
   * framework strips it.
   */
  basePath?: string;
  /** Largest accepted request body. Default 10 MB. */
  maxBodyBytes?: number;
  /**
   * Reject targets on loopback, private, link-local and cloud-metadata addresses (IP literals,
   * `localhost`, `*.local`, `*.internal`), so a public endpoint can't be aimed at your internal
   * network. Hostnames that *resolve* to private IPs are not caught; with a proxy provider, the
   * proxy's network is what's reachable anyway. Default false; `xyte serve` turns it on.
   */
  blockPrivateTargets?: boolean;
  /**
   * `POST /v1/jobs` (a Zyte request plus an optional `callbackUrl`) answers `202 { id, status }`
   * at once; `GET /v1/jobs/{id}` returns the job, with the Zyte response when `done`; the
   * result is POSTed to `callbackUrl` when it finishes. Options: where jobs are kept, for how
   * long, the webhook secret. `false` turns the routes off. On by default, in memory.
   */
  jobs?: JobsOptions | false;
  /**
   * `GET /api/stats` and `/api/v1/stats` in the shape of Zyte's Stats API, from the requests this
   * handler served (extract and jobs). Pass a recorder to share it (e.g. with a Redis store, or to
   * also `record()` library requests); `false` turns the routes off. On by default, in memory.
   */
  stats?: StatsRecorder | false;
}
```

### `FetchHandler`

A Web-standard request handler, as `Bun.serve`, Deno, Hono and Workers take.

```ts
type FetchHandler = (request: Request) => Promise<Response>;
```

### `toNodeHandler`

Adapts a fetch handler to Node's `(req, res)` signature, for `node:http`, Express, Fastify
(`reply.hijack()` first) or Next.js API routes:

    app.use('/zyte', toNodeHandler(createHandler(xyte)));

A body already parsed by middleware (e.g. `express.json()`) is re-serialized.

```ts
function toNodeHandler(handler: FetchHandler, options?: {
  maxBodyBytes?: number;
}): (req: IncomingMessage & {
  body?: unknown;
}, res: ServerResponse) => Promise<void>;
```

### `serve`

Serves `handler` on Bun (`Bun.serve`) or Node.js (`node:http`). Returns a function that stops
the server.

```ts
function serve(handler: FetchHandler, options?: {
  port?: number;
  hostname?: string;
}): Promise<{
  url: string;
  stop: () => Promise<void>;
}>;
```

### `isPrivateTarget`

Loopback, RFC 1918, link-local (incl. 169.254.169.254), CGNAT, ULA, and internal names.

```ts
function isPrivateTarget(target: string): boolean;
```

### `Jobs`

Runs requests in the background (`POST /v1/jobs`): `submit()` answers at once with a job, `get()` reads it
later, and a `callbackUrl` gets the result POSTed, signed (see `verifyWebhook`).

```ts
class Jobs {
  constructor(xyte: Xyte, options?: JobsOptions);
  /** Queues a request and starts it in the background; resolves with the queued job. */
  submit(request: ExtractRequest, callbackUrl?: string): Promise<Job>;
  /** The job as it is now; undefined if unknown, or older than `ttl`. */
  get(id: string): Promise<Job | undefined>;
}
```

### `Job`

An asynchronous job, as `POST /v1/jobs` and `GET /v1/jobs/{id}` return it.

```ts
interface Job {
  id: string;
  status: "queued" | "running" | "done" | "failed";
  createdAt: string;
  startedAt?: string;
  finishedAt?: string;
  /** The Zyte response, when `done`. */
  response?: ExtractResponse;
  /** The Zyte problem, when `failed`. */
  error?: XyteProblem;
  callbackUrl?: string;
  /** How the webhook delivery went. */
  callback?: {
    status: "pending" | "delivered" | "failed";
    attempts: number;
    lastError?: string;
  };
}
```

### `JobsOptions`

Asynchronous extraction: submit a request, get an id back at once, and fetch the result later
or have it POSTed to a webhook. For renders that outlast an HTTP timeout, and for queues.

```ts
interface JobsOptions {
  /** Where jobs are kept. Default: this process's memory. Redis lets any instance answer a job's status. */
  store?: StateStore;
  /** Seconds a job (and its result) is kept. Default 86400 (a day). */
  ttl?: number;
  /** Signs webhook deliveries: `X-Xyte-Signature: sha256=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of the body>`. */
  webhookSecret?: string;
  /** Webhook delivery attempts. Default 3, backing off 1 s, 2 s… */
  webhookAttempts?: number;
  /** For webhook deliveries (tests, proxies). */
  fetch?: typeof fetch;
  /** Each job's request report (the server feeds its stats with it). */
  onReport?: (report: RequestReport) => void;
}
```

### `verifyWebhook`

Verifies a webhook delivery's `X-Xyte-Signature` against the raw body.

```ts
function verifyWebhook(body: string, signature: string | null | undefined, secret: string): boolean;
```

### `StatsRecorder`

Records each request's report and answers Zyte's Stats API queries over them (`GET /api/stats`).
Keeps hourly buckets in a store, so with Redis every instance reports the same totals.

```ts
class StatsRecorder {
  constructor(options?: StatsOptions);
  /** Adds a request; flushed to the store within a second. */
  record(report: RequestReport, at?: Date): void;
  /** Writes pending counts to the store (read, add, write per hour). */
  flush(): Promise<void>;
  /**
   * Stats in Zyte's shape. `currencies: 'v1'` gives `/api/v1/stats`'s per-currency `cost_micro_*`
   * arrays; otherwise `/api/stats`'s `cost_microusd_*` strings. Throws a 422-style Error for an
   * invalid query.
   */
  query(query: StatsQuery, format?: "usd" | "v1"): Promise<StatsResponse>;
}
```

### `StatsOptions`

Usage stats in the shape of Zyte's Stats API (https://docs.zyte.com/zyte-api/usage/stats/),
built from request reports: so a dashboard or a billing check written for Zyte reads xyte's
numbers by changing its base URL. `record()` takes `RequestReport`s (`onRequest`); `query()`
answers `/api/stats` and `/api/v1/stats` parameters.

```ts
interface StatsOptions {
  /** Where hourly buckets are kept. Default: this process's memory. Redis adds up every instance. */
  store?: StateStore;
  /** Days of stats kept. Default 31. */
  retentionDays?: number;
  /** The `organization_id` reported. Default 0; a query's own is echoed back. */
  organizationId?: number;
}
```

### `StatsQuery`

The query parameters of `GET /api/stats`, as on Zyte.

```ts
interface StatsQuery {
  organization_id?: string | number;
  start_time?: string;
  end_time?: string;
  page?: string | number;
  page_size?: string | number;
  /** Comma-separated hosts. */
  domains?: string;
  /** Comma-separated codes (`200,404`). */
  response_codes?: string;
  /** Comma-separated `tag:value` (that value) or `tag` (present), all required. */
  tags?: string;
  groupby_time?: "hour" | "day" | "month" | "year" | null;
  groupby_domain?: string | boolean;
  include_domain_health?: string | boolean;
}
```

### `StatsResponse`

The Stats API's answer, in Zyte's shape.

```ts
interface StatsResponse {
  page: number;
  page_size: number;
  results: Record<string, unknown>[];
  total_result_count: number;
}
```

### `StatsQueryError`

An invalid Stats API query: the server answers it with a 400.

```ts
class StatsQueryError extends Error {}
```

### `serveProxyMode`

A proxy-mode server on its own port.

```ts
function serveProxyMode(xyte: Xyte, options?: ProxyModeOptions & {
  port?: number;
  hostname?: string;
}): Promise<{
  port: number;
  caCert: string;
  stop: () => Promise<void>;
}>;
```

### `attachProxyMode`

Adds proxy mode to a node:http server: absolute-URL requests (http://) and CONNECT tunnels
(https://, decrypted with per-site certificates from the CA). Returns the CA's certificate.

```ts
function attachProxyMode(server: Server, xyte: Xyte, options?: ProxyModeOptions): {
  caCert: string;
};
```

### `ProxyModeOptions`

Zyte API's proxy mode (https://docs.zyte.com/zyte-api/usage/proxy-mode.html), served by xyte:
clients use it as an HTTP proxy (`curl -x xyte:8012 -U key: --cacert ca.crt https://site`),
options go in `Zyte-*` request headers, and the answer is the site's own response. HTTPS is
decrypted with a certificate signed by the proxy's CA, which clients must trust, as with Zyte's.

```ts
interface ProxyModeOptions {
  /** Accepted keys, as the proxy username (`Proxy-Authorization: Basic base64(key:)`). Empty: anyone. */
  apiKeys?: readonly string[];
  /** The CA that signs per-site certificates. Default: a new one (clients must trust it, so keep one). */
  ca?: CertificateAuthority;
  /** Reject targets on loopback, private and metadata addresses. */
  blockPrivateTargets?: boolean;
  /** Each request's report (for stats or logs). */
  onReport?: (report: RequestReport) => void;
}
```

### `proxiedRequest`

The Zyte request a proxied request stands for: its URL, method, body, headers and `Zyte-*` options.

```ts
function proxiedRequest(url: string, method: string, headers: IncomingMessage["headers"], body: Buffer): ExtractRequest;
```

### `createCertificateAuthority`

A new CA (10 years). Keep it: clients trust this one certificate.

```ts
function createCertificateAuthority(commonName?: string): CertificateAuthority;
```

### `issueCertificate`

A certificate for `host` (a name or an IP), signed by the CA, valid for a year.

```ts
function issueCertificate(ca: CertificateAuthority, host: string): {
  cert: string;
  key: string;
};
```

### `CertificateAuthority`

A certificate authority for proxy mode, as Zyte has one: to apply bans, retries and providers
to HTTPS traffic, the proxy must read it, so it presents a certificate for each site signed by
this CA, which clients are told to trust. Built with node:crypto (P-256 keys, ECDSA-SHA256) and a
minimal DER encoder, no dependencies.

```ts
interface CertificateAuthority {
  /** PEM certificate: what clients install (curl --cacert, NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS, REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE…). */
  cert: string;
  /** PEM private key: keep it secret; anyone holding it can impersonate sites to those clients. */
  key: string;
}
```

## Configuration from the environment

What the CLI builds from `process.env`; each takes an `env` to read instead. [Configuration](configuration.md#environment-variables).

### `proxyFromEnv`

Builds the proxy from environment variables:

- `XYTE_PROXY_URL`: one or more proxy URLs, comma-separated (rotated across retries), or
- `XYTE_PROXY_TEMPLATE`: a `template()` format, e.g.
  `http://user-{env:MY_USER}[-country-{country:lower}]-session-{session}:{env:MY_PASS}@host:7000`, or
- `XYTE_PROVIDER`: one or more provider names, comma-separated (a retry moves to the next one),
  each with its credentials (`OXYLABS_USERNAME`, `ZENROWS_API_KEY`, …). See `PROVIDER_NAMES` and
  docs/providers.md, or
- `XYTE_ADAPTIVE`: provider names, cheapest first, for `adaptive()`.

Neither set: no proxy. On top of that:

- `XYTE_ROUTES=doordash.com=zyte-api,wolt.com=direct,restaurantguru.com=oxylabs+zyte-api`: a
  provider per site (`route()`), `+` rotating; other sites use the above.
- `XYTE_BROWSER_PROVIDER`: provider names for browser renders (`byKind()`).
- `XYTE_CIRCUIT_BREAKER=5,60`: wraps every named provider in `healthy()` (failures, cooldown s).
- `XYTE_BUDGET=zyte-api=500/hour,scrapingbee=1000/day`: wraps those providers in `budget()`.
- `XYTE_WATCH=true`: wraps providers that have a usage API or status page in `watch()`
  (`XYTE_WATCH_EVERY` seconds, default 60). Oxylabs needs `OXYLABS_LIMIT_GB` (and, if the
  proxy user isn't the account's main one, `OXYLABS_API_USERNAME` / `OXYLABS_API_PASSWORD`).
- `XYTE_REDIS_URL=redis://…`: budgets, circuits and checks are shared by every instance.

A provider named in several places is one instance, so its budget and circuit are shared.

```ts
function proxyFromEnv(env?: Env): ProxyProvider;
```

### `browserFromEnv`

Browser settings from environment variables:

- `XYTE_BROWSER`: `playwright` (default), a stealth preset (`patchright`, `rebrowser`, `camoufox`,
  `cloakbrowser`), or any installed Playwright-compatible package name exporting `chromium`.
- `XYTE_BROWSER_CHANNEL`: e.g. `chrome` to use installed Google Chrome.
- `XYTE_BROWSER_HEADLESS=false`: headed (needs a display, e.g. xvfb).
- `XYTE_BROWSER_ARGS`: extra Chromium flags, comma-separated.
- `XYTE_REMOTE_BROWSER`: a hosted browser preset: `brightdata`, `browserless`, `zenrows`, `oxylabs`,
  `nodemaven` (with its credentials, see docs/browser.md), or
- `XYTE_BROWSER_WS`: render in a remote browser at this CDP endpoint instead; accepts the same
  placeholders as `XYTE_PROXY_TEMPLATE` (e.g. `{country:lower}`, `{session}`).
  `XYTE_BROWSER_WS_PROTOCOL=playwright` for a Playwright server.
- `XYTE_BLOCK_RESOURCES`: resource types to abort, e.g. `image,media,font`.
- `XYTE_BROWSER_TIME_LIMIT`: seconds per request (default 60).
- `XYTE_BROWSER_SETTLE`: seconds to wait for the network to go quiet after load (default 3, 0 to skip).

```ts
function browserFromEnv(env?: Env): BrowserOptions;
```

### `extractorsFromEnv`

AI extraction from environment variables (any OpenAI-compatible API):
`XYTE_LLM_MODEL` (required to enable), `XYTE_LLM_BASE_URL` (default OpenAI), `XYTE_LLM_API_KEY`,
`XYTE_LLM_RESPONSE_FORMAT=json_object` for servers without JSON-schema output. Unset: no AI
extraction (those fields get a 400, as without an extractor).

```ts
function extractorsFromEnv(env?: Env): Partial<Record<ExtractionField, Extractor>> | undefined;
```

### `cacheFromEnv`

The response cache from `XYTE_CACHE_TTL`: seconds for every site (`3600`), or per site
(`wolt.com=600,*=3600`). Shared through `XYTE_REDIS_URL` when set. Unset: no cache.

```ts
function cacheFromEnv(env?: Env): CacheOptions | undefined;
```

### `rateLimitsFromEnv`

Per-site pacing from `XYTE_RATE_LIMITS`: `yelp.co.uk=2/s,doordash.com=30/m,*=10/s`.

```ts
function rateLimitsFromEnv(env?: Env): RateLimits | undefined;
```

### `ratesFromEnv`

Your prices from `XYTE_RATES`: `oxylabs=6/GB,zyte-api=0.0013/request,scrapingbee=0.0005/success`,
`+` to combine units for one provider (`x=2/GB+0.001/request`).

```ts
function ratesFromEnv(env?: Env): Rates | undefined;
```

### `sessionsFromEnv`

The `sessionContext` pool from the environment: shared through `XYTE_REDIS_URL` when set.

```ts
function sessionsFromEnv(env?: Env): SessionPoolOptions | undefined;
```

### `jobsFromEnv`

The server's job options: `XYTE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `XYTE_JOBS_TTL` (seconds), kept in `XYTE_REDIS_URL` when set.

```ts
function jobsFromEnv(env?: Env): JobsOptions;
```

### `statsFromEnv`

The server's stats: kept in `XYTE_REDIS_URL` when set (every instance adds up), else in memory.

```ts
function statsFromEnv(env?: Env): StatsRecorder;
```

### `caFromEnv`

Proxy mode's CA: `XYTE_CA_CERT` / `XYTE_CA_KEY` (PEM, or paths to PEM files), else the one in
`XYTE_CA_DIR` (default `~/.xyte`), created there on first use. It must stay the same across
restarts and instances: clients trust this certificate.

```ts
function caFromEnv(env?: Env): Promise<{
  ca: CertificateAuthority;
  source: string;
}>;
```

### `closeSharedStores`

Closes the Redis connections the `*FromEnv` helpers opened for `XYTE_REDIS_URL` (one per URL,
shared by all of them). Call it on shutdown, after `xyte.close()`: on Node with `ioredis` or
`redis`, an open connection keeps the process from exiting.

```ts
function closeSharedStores(): Promise<void>;
```

## Tools

`xyte doctor`'s checks, as functions.

### `doctor`

Checks each provider end to end: its credentials are there, a request through it works (and
exits where it should), and its quota or status, where it has a usage API or status page.

```ts
function doctor(options?: DoctorOptions): Promise<DoctorResult[]>;
```

### `formatDoctor`

The results as a table for a terminal.

```ts
function formatDoctor(results: readonly DoctorResult[]): string;
```

### `DoctorOptions`

Options of `doctor()`: what to check, and how.

```ts
interface DoctorOptions {
  env?: Record<string, string | undefined>;
  /** Provider names (`XYTE_PROVIDER` names, or `direct`). Default: `direct` plus every one the environment configures. */
  providers?: readonly string[];
  /** What to fetch through each. Default `https://ipinfo.io/json`, which reports the exit IP and country. */
  url?: string;
  /** `geolocation` for the probe, to check providers apply it. */
  country?: string;
  /** Seconds per probe. Default 30. */
  timeout?: number;
}
```

### `DoctorResult`

What `doctor()` found for one provider.

```ts
interface DoctorResult {
  provider: string;
  ok: boolean;
  /** The exit the probe saw (with the default probe URL, ipinfo.io's answer). */
  ip?: string;
  country?: string;
  city?: string;
  org?: string;
  ms?: number;
  /** Why it failed: missing credentials, rejected credentials, unreachable… */
  error?: string;
  /** A note that doesn't fail it, e.g. the exit country isn't the one asked for. */
  note?: string;
  /** Its usage API or status page, where it has one. */
  quota?: CheckResult | {
    error: string;
  };
}
```
